Answer: D
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates right lung volume loss with mediastinal shift to the right and compensatory hyperaeration of the remaining lobes (specifically the middle and lower lobes appearing expanded), which are characteristic findings of right upper lobe hypoplasia. The "kinked" vessel appearance is often associated with the anomalous vascular anatomy seen in such developmental anomalies, but the overall pattern of volume loss without complete agenesis supports hypoplasia.
